name: How do I know if my pool is gunite, fiberglass, or vinyl before removal?

mainEntity.name: Why does the pool material matter, and how can I identify it before getting quotes?
mainEntity.text: Why does the pool material matter, and how can I identify it before getting quotes?

acceptedAnswer.text: Pool material is one of the first things a contractor needs to estimate removal cost correctly. Gunite and concrete pools are typically the most labor-intensive because they are thick, reinforced, and heavy to break and haul. Fiberglass pools are different because the shell often needs to be excavated in larger pieces. Vinyl pools are usually simpler because the liner and supporting frame can be removed with less demolition. Homeowners can often spot clues by looking at the edge detail, shell thickness, surface texture, and whether the pool sounds hollow or solid when tapped. If there is any uncertainty, a site visit is the best way to avoid a bad estimate. A contractor should explain how the material changes the removal method, disposal volume, and restoration plan. That helps prevent surprise charges once work begins.
acceptedAnswer.description: Pool material affects demolition cost, disposal, and equipment needs. Gunite and concrete are usually the hardest to remove, fiberglass is lighter but may require large shell extraction, and vinyl pools often involve liner and frame removal. The finish, edge shape, and shell thickness help identify the type.
